samples.summary: Flipping YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE to enforce-by-default activates a documented, unmitigated denial risk for existing deployments that already registered the webhook methods
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21) makes an unset variable mean *enforce*. The out-of-diff rollout contract this changes is recorded at docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283: "A viewer ... client that still emits a local change on load ... → verb `rw` → the webhook denies it under enforcement. The React `DocumentProvider` does not currently expose a read-only/`syncMode` attach option, so this can't be forced from the frontend today. **Mitigation:** shadow mode is exactly the instrument for this — the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping ... =true." That mitigation is exactly what the new default removes: any deployment that already ran `--auth-webhook-method-add AttachDocument/PushPull` while relying on the shadow default (the state packages/backend/README.md:252-256 and docs/design/sharing.md:208 describe as the stock one) starts denying on upgrade, with no config change of its own, and the SDK-level fix the design doc names as the precondition is still a follow-up. Nothing in the diff addresses the migration for those installs; the only other consumers given a token were the backend's own clients.

samples.summary: Several out-of-diff comments and design docs still state that the auth webhook "ships in shadow mode by default", which is now false — including ones that conclude client-side read-only is therefore the write boundary
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 ("the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary"); packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413 ("shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock ..."); docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 and 231-235 ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode"); docs/design/template-gallery.md:668; docs/design/revision-history.md:504; docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301; docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:279-281. The diff even reintroduces the stale claim inside the new code it touches: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:~450 says "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", contradicting packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64 in the same PR. Nested design docs are not covered by the docs link check, so nothing else will flag these.

samples.summary: The share-link notes mount reuses the docs uploader, whose failure contract (reject) differs from the notes `UploadImage` contract (resolve `null` after telling the user), so a failed image upload on a shared note is silent
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` is typed `DocsImageUpload = (file: File) => Promise<string>` and rejects on failure with no user-facing report (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:15,40-49) — its docs callers surface the error via `insertImageFromFile`/toast. The notes contract is different: `UploadImage = (file) => Promise<string | null>` (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:26) documented at packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:47-50 as "`null` if the upload failed and was already reported to the user", and the engine swallows a rejection into `console.error` only (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-190). The workspace route honours that contract by catching and toasting (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:203-215). So an editor-role visitor whose upload is rejected (size/type/expired token) sees the placeholder vanish with no message. Frontend has no `tsc`, so the type-compatible-but-semantically-different reuse is not caught anywhere.

samples.summary: Checked-in compiled copies of the migration/copy scripts were not regenerated, so they still build anonymous Yorkie clients and will now be denied wherever the webhook methods are registered
samples.evidence: packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.js:162 still constructs the source client with `apiKey` only and no `authTokenInjector` (the compiled sibling packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.js is likewise stale). The documented invocation is via `tsx` on the `.ts` (packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:30), so this is a divergence rather than a break in the sanctioned path — but the stale artifacts are the exact anonymous-attach shape the diff set out to remove, and `node scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.js` now fails against any enforcing deployment.

samples.summary: Read-only mounts now publish no local selection, so a viewer's caret disappears from peers on every read-only notes mount (share link and revision preview)
samples.evidence: `initialize` wraps the store for read-only mounts (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:~240) and `readOnlyNoteStore` no-ops `setLocalSelection` deliberately (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:138-142). The out-of-diff consumer is packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:170-172, which published the local caret for every mount including read-only ones — so peers of a viewer-role share-link visitor lose that caret. Intended per the wrapper's comment, and harmless, but it is a behaviour change at a call site outside the diff and is not mentioned in the notes design doc's presence section.

finding.summary: Flipping YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE to enforce-by-default activates a documented, unmitigated denial risk for existing deployments that already registered the webhook methods
finding.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21) makes an unset variable mean *enforce*. The out-of-diff rollout contract this changes is recorded at docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283: "A viewer ... client that still emits a local change on load ... → verb `rw` → the webhook denies it under enforcement. That mitigation is exactly what the new default removes: any deployment that already ran `--auth-webhook-method-add AttachDocument/PushPull` while relying on the shadow default (the state packages/backend/README.md:252-256 and docs/design/sharing.md:208 describe as the stock one) starts denying on upgrade, with no config change of its own, and the SDK-level fix the design doc names as the precondition is still a follow-up. verdict.reason:
The core of the finding checks out in the repository. `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22) returns true for anything except the literal string `false`, so an unset `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` now means *enforce*; the controller consumes it directly (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:133-137) and, when enforcing, returns the computed denial verbatim (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:168-187) instead of the previous allow-all shadow response. The design doc's own comment at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:114-117 confirms the out-of-diff consumer this affects: registering the Yorkie project's webhook methods is a separate manual deployment step, so any install that already ran `--auth-webhook-method-add …` while leaving the variable unset silently changes posture from allow-everything to deny-on-computed-denial on upgrade, with no config change of its own.

The rollout contract the finding quotes is present verbatim at docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283, including "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`" and "the fix is a read-only attach path in the SDK wrapper (follow-up)". That paragraph is now internally inconsistent with the new default described in the same file at lines 240-250, and the risk it names is still unresolved: the shared viewer route mounts plain `DocumentProvider`s with no read-only/`syncMode` option (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:955-1027), and no non-test `syncMode`/read-only attach exists on the frontend path (only backend REST readers pass `syncMode: 'readonly'`, e.g. packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:56).

I checked for a guard that would make this unreachable and found only a partial one: `docsInitialRootForRole` / `notesInitialRootForRole` / `boardInitialRootForRole` / `sheetsInitialRootForRole` return `{}` for viewers (shared-document.tsx:974, 992, 1007, 1020; packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.test.ts:39), which removes the root-seeding write on viewer attach. That does not cover the other change sources the doc names, and the repo's own risk register still records the verb question as open, so it is not `already-guarded`. Two ancillary evidence citations in the finding are inaccurate — packages/backend/README.md:252-256 has already been updated to describe enforce-as-default, though docs/design/sharing.md:208 ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment") does still describe shadow as stock — but that inaccuracy does not overturn the substance. Under the blast-radius rubric this is a behaviour change to a config contract whose existing consumers (deployments with the methods registered, plus the un-updated viewer attach path) were not migrated, so it stays.

finding.summary: Backend ops scripts attach to Yorkie with no auth token, so this delta's own premise (enforcement is the default; an absent token is refused) leaves them broken on any deployment that registered the webhook methods
finding.evidence: `packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:214` `const client = new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey });` — no `authTokenInjector`. Same at `packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:340` and `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:204,208`. All then `activate()` + `attach()` documents. The first two are reachable as `pnpm migrate:yorkie:cf-ranges` / `migrate:yorkie:worksheet-shape` (packages/backend/package.json:28-29). The fix belongs in these scripts (mint via `signYorkieServiceToken` from the new `src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts`), which is exactly the remedy this delta applied to `YorkieService`.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false at all three cited locations. Each ops script constructs its yorkie.Client WITH an authTokenInjector minted by the exact helper the finding proposes as the fix: migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221 (`authTokenInjector: yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv()`, import at line 3), migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347 (import at line 9), and copy-yorkie-documents.ts:232 and :238 for the source and target clients respectively, each passed its own side's JWT secret (import at line 5). The reviewer's quoted line numbers (214, 340, 204/208) point at the adjacent rpcAddr/apiKey reads; the injector sits a few lines below in the same object literal, which is why a grep for `new Client(`/`rpcAddr` alone would not surface it. The helper exists as packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts:75-87 (`yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv`, reading process.env.JWT_SECRET / YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN) wrapping `signYorkieServiceToken` at line 38, and its doc comment at lines 64-74 states it exists specifically for the ops scripts under packages/backend/scripts. The reachable pnpm entry points (packages/backend/package.json:28-29) run `tsx` against the .ts files that carry the injector, not the stale compiled .js artifacts beside them, and no package.json script invokes those .js files. Only the missing-secret branch leaves a client anonymous, which is an intentional warn-not-throw fallback for local Yorkie without registered webhook methods, not the claimed omission.
